## Overview: The Ideal Op-Amp Golden Rules

In operational amplifier circuit analysis, negative feedback networks are analyzed rapidly by applying the two **ideal op-amp assumptions** (often called the *Golden Rules*):

1. **Infinite Open-Loop Gain ($A_{ol} \to \infty$):** When an op-amp operates in its linear region with negative feedback, the voltage difference between the non-inverting and inverting input terminals is driven to zero (a *virtual short*):
   $$\mathbf{V_+ = V_-}$$

2. **Infinite Input Impedance ($R_{in} \to \infty$):** Because the input stage draws negligible current, the current entering both the non-inverting and inverting terminals is zero:
   $$\mathbf{I_+ = I_- = 0\text{ A}}$$

## Summary of Standard Closed-Loop Topologies

Before testing AC waveform clipping and completing the design challenges in Part 2, review how Kirchhoff's Current Law (KCL) at the inverting node ($V_-$) yields the closed-loop gain for each standard configuration:

| Topology | Node Voltage ($V_+ = V_-$) | Ideal Closed-Loop Output ($V_{out}$) | Input Impedance ($Z_{in}$) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Non-Inverting** | $V_- = V_{in}$ | $V_{out} = V_{in}\left(1 + \dfrac{R_f}{R_{in}}\right)$ | $\infty$ (Extremely High) |
| **Inverting** | $V_- = 0\text{ V}$ *(Virtual Ground)* | $V_{out} = -\left(\dfrac{R_f}{R_{in}}\right)V_{in}$ | $R_{in}$ |
| **Summing Mixer** | $V_- = 0\text{ V}$ *(Virtual Ground)* | $V_{out} = -R_f\left(\dfrac{V_1}{R_1} + \dfrac{V_2}{R_2}\right)$ | $R_1, R_2$ per channel |
| **Difference (Matched)** | $V_- = V_2\left(\dfrac{R_4}{R_3 + R_4}\right)$ | $V_{out} = \dfrac{R_f}{R_1}\left(V_2 - V_1\right)$ | $R_1$ (Inverting) |
| **Unity Buffer** | $V_- = V_{in}$ | $V_{out} = V_{in}$ ($A_v = 1$) | $\infty$ (Impedance Isolator) |

## Part 2: AC Waveform Clipping & Design Verification Lab

Real operational amplifiers cannot output voltages beyond their DC power supply rails ($+V_{CC}$ and $-V_{EE}$). Whenever the ideal mathematical output exceeds these limits, the output stage saturates and **clips** the waveform. 

Use the virtual oscilloscope below to inspect sinusoidal, triangular, and square wave amplification, complete the **5 progressive design challenges**, and export your verified circuit directly to **LTspice (`.cir`)** or **LaTeX (`circuitikz`)**.
